title: soft headroom redistributor and cross-cluster warm-queue
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: reserve-heavy tenants and uneven cluster packing are causing long periods of underutilized Dedicated capacity while other clusters experience microburst shortages. This PR introduces a conservative, safety-first mechanism to opportunistically redistribute soft headroom (unused burst credits and pre-warmed slot budgets) across compatible clusters and a cross-cluster warm-queue that proactively pre-warms warmlets on low-utilization racks. Goals: (1) reduce wasted reserved dollars, (2) improve tail throughput for tenants that experience transient surges, (3) maintain strict isolation and safety so no tenant's committed capacity is violated.

Summary of changes: (single continuous description) Implemented HeadroomRedistributor controller that periodically samples per-cluster headroom signals and offers redistributable credit parcels. Added CrossClusterWarmQueue that enqueues warm tasks with affinity and rack-safety rules; warmlets are scheduled with a capped evictable token so they yield under pressure. Updated autoscaler decision path to consult redistributor signals before making scale-down/scale-up choices. New telemetry: redistributable_headroom_bytes, redistributed_parcels_count, warmqueue_pending, warmlet_prewarms_succeeded, warmlet_evictions. Introduced a conservative 3-stage safety check: (a) commitment-guard ensures tenant-commitment watermark isn't affected, (b) locality-guard prevents cross-region redistribution, (c) reclaim-policy ensures distributed headroom is recalled within configured windows.

Testing and rollout plan: added unit tests around the redistributor state machine and warm-queue backpressure. Added an integration test harness that spins a 3-cluster simulator with synthetic burst traffic; this is gated behind a slow-integration CI job. Rollout strategy: feature-flagged off by default, enable for internal staging clusters for 2 weeks (traffic experiments), then enable for low-risk customers with canary ratio 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Metrics dashboards and alerts are included.

Notes: this PR purposefully decouples the redistributor from the primary autoscaler to keep operational boundaries clear; operators can disable redistribution without changing scaling rules. See linked Linear items for experiment tracking and acceptance criteria.

Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (ENG-3211) - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration test added (slow) - [x] telemetry wired to metrics pipeline - [x] feature flag gating the controllers

Related: ENG-3211, ENG-3287, incident SUP-78 referenced for burst hotspot investigation.

review_comments: Daniel Kim (2026-02-09): This looks promising. Two concerns: race between recall window and autoscaler ramp-down, and how redistributor offers interact with preemption on spot nodes. Please add a unit test that simulates a recall during a scale-down decision.

Priya Shah (2026-02-10): Added a recall-unit test and a recall hook that is consulted by the autoscaler. Spot preemption is handled by the reclaim-policy which tags parcels as evictable; updated docs to clarify. PTAL.

Ruth Alvarez (2026-02-11): Please ensure telemetry cardinality is bounded; the current reporter emits one metric per tenant+cluster. Suggest aggregating to cluster-level and tagging by tenant percentile. Also add an alert for sustained recall cycles.
Priya Shah (2026-02-12): Aggregated metrics to cluster-level and added percentile tagging. Added alert rule: 'redistributor.recall_cycles > 3 over 5m -> page'.
Samir Nair (2026-02-13): Left one nit in the warmlet scheduler regarding exponential backoff defaults. Also requested a brief canary playbook for operations.
Priya Shah (2026-02-14): Addressed nit, added canary playbook to runbook. Tests passing locally; pushing CI fix for a flake in integration harness.

release_notes: Introduce a feature-flagged soft headroom redistributor and cross-cluster warm-queue to improve utilization across Dedicated clusters. Operators can enable via deploy/featureflags/soft_headroom.yaml. New metrics: redistributable_headroom_bytes, redistributed_parcels_count, warmqueue_pending, warmlet_prewarms_succeeded. Safeguards include commitment-guard, locality-guard, and a reclaim-policy. Rollout: staged canary; disabled by default.
